items.title: The neuroscience of delirium: a perfect storm for acute brain dysfunction
items.author: Eyal Kimchi
items.content: Delirium is a highly prevalent, but much neglected, acute neuropsychiatric syndrome strongly associated with dementia. In this Review, Cunningham and Kimchi detail the neurophysiological and neuroanatomical basis of delirium and the metabolic and neuroinflammatory mechanisms that may drive it.

items.title: The many facets of human brain asymmetry
items.author: Clyde Francks
items.content: Contrasting the right and left hemisphere has undergone a methodological and conceptual transformation. In this Review, Francks and colleagues focus on brain asymmetry as a multivariate and multiscale organizational feature of the human brain while discussing its variability across individuals and how left–right asymmetry supports cognition and behaviour.

items.title: Network approaches to community detection in nanoscale connectomics
items.author: Richard Betzel
items.content: Extracting insight from nanoscale connectomes presents formidable challenges. In this Review, Betzel and colleagues focus on network science applications to these high-dimensional datasets, providing a high-level overview of different community detection methods while discussing which methods suit which questions and the types of biologically meaningful information they can reveal.

items.title: The cortico-basal ganglia–thalamic network: a connectomic framework
items.author: Houri Hintiryan
items.content: The cortico-basal ganglia–thalamic (CBGT) system supports a wide range of behaviours through its modular network organization. Dong and colleagues describe how advanced mesoscale and single-neuron connectomics has refined our understanding of CBGT circuit architecture, providing insights into the network’s capacity to preserve functional specialization while integrating across sensory, motor and cognitive domains.

items.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of cellular heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease
items.author: Vivek Swarup
items.content: Single-cell and single-nucleus RNA sequencing technologies have advanced our understanding of the molecular responses of specific cellular populations to Alzheimer disease (AD). Swarup and colleagues outline the insights that these approaches have provided into the multicellular interactions that underlie AD pathogenesis and heterogeneity.

items.title: The nanotubular network as a new dimension of intercellular communication in the nervous system
items.author: Hyung-Bae Kwon
items.content: Intercellular nanotubes (NTs) provide a structurally distinct route of intercellular communication by enabling cellular material to be selectively transferred between cells. In this Review, Chang, Ryu and Kwon discuss the evidence for NT networks in the nervous system and the experimental approaches that can be used to study NTs in this context.

items.title: Sleep-sensitive neurons mediate consolidation
items.author: Katherine Whalley
items.content: A population of acetylcholine-sensitive GABAergic neurons in the mouse hippocampus regulates sharp wave ripples and memory consolidation during sleep.

items.title: Interneurons and network activity in the cerebral cortex: a developmental dialogue
items.author: Oscar Marín
items.content: Neuronal activity is traditionally viewed as instructing cortical interneuron development. In this Review, Moissidis and Marín discuss how interneurons also actively shape early postnatal network activity, establishing a reciprocal dialogue that drives the maturation of both interneurons and cortical circuits.
